'''''Disphyma''''' is a genus of flowering plants in the family [[Aizoaceae]] that are native to New Zealand, Australia, and the [[Cape Provinces]] of South Africa. Plants in this genus are [[Prostrate shrub|prostrate]], [[Annual plant|annual]] or short-lived [[Perennial plant|perennial]] shrubs with [[Succulent plant|succulent]] leaves and daisy-like flowers arranged singly on the ends of shoots with petal-like [[staminode]]s, many [[stamen]]s and usually five [[Style (botany)|styles]].

==Description==
Plants in the genus ''Disphyma'' are prostrate, annual plants or short-lived perennials with branches that root at [[Plant stem|nodes]]. The leaves are arranged alternately and fused at the base, succulent and round to more or less triangular in cross-section. The flowers are usually arranged singly, sometimes in pairs or three, on the ends of branches or on short side shoots, each flower on a [[Pedicel (botany)|pedicel]] up to {{cvt|100|mm}} long. The [[perianth]] is tube-shaped with five [[sepal]]s, two larger and leaf-like and three smaller, slightly succulent and not leaf-like. There are many petal-like, purplish staminodes in two rows and many [[stamen]]s in four or five rows. The [[Ovary (botany)|ovary]] is [[Ovary (botany)#Inferior ovary|inferior]] and there are usually five [[Style (botany)|styles]]. The fruit is a [[Capsule (botany)|capsule]].<ref name="RBGV">{{cite web |last1=Walsh |first1=Neville G. |title=''Disphyma'' |url=https://vicflora.rbg.vic.gov.au/flora/taxon/2b758014-828d-4076-806c-120bbb6795be |publisher=Royal Botanic Gardens Victoria |access-date=17 October 2020}}</ref><ref name="RBGS">{{cite web |last1=Jacobs |first1=Surrey Wilfrid Laurance |last2=Highet |first2=Jeannie |title=Genus ''Disphyma'' |url=https://plantnet.rbgsyd.nsw.gov.au/cgi-bin/NSWfl.pl?page=nswfl&showsyn=&dist=&constat=&lvl=gn&name=Disphyma |publisher=Royal Botanic Garden Sydney |access-date=17 October 2020}}</ref>

==Taxonomy==
The genus ''Disphyma'' was first formally described in 1925 by [[N. E. Brown]] in ''[[The Gardeners' Chronicle]]''.<ref name=APNI1>{{cite web|title=''Disphyma''|url= https://id.biodiversity.org.au/instance/apni/488030|publisher=APNI|access-date=17 October 2020}}</ref><ref name="POWO">{{cite web |title=''Disphyma'' N.E.Br. |url=https://powo.science.kew.org/taxon/urn:lsid:ipni.org:names:16167-1 |publisher=Plants of the World Online |access-date=17 October 2020}}</ref>

As at October 2020, [[Plants of the World Online]] accepts four species:
* ''[[Disphyma australe]]'' <small>([[Sol.]] ex [[William Aiton|Aiton]]) [[J.M.Black]]</small> that is [[Endemism|endemic]] to New Zealand;<ref name="POWO1">{{cite web |title=''Disphyma australe'' (Sol. ex Aiton) J.M.Black |url=https://powo.science.kew.org/taxon/urn:lsid:ipni.org:names:361625-1 |publisher=Plants of the World Online |access-date=17 October 2020}}</ref>
* ''[[Disphyma crassifolium]]'' <small>([[Carl Linnaeus|L.]]) [[L.Bolus]]</small> that is native to Australia and the [[Cape Province]] in southern Africa;<ref name="POWO2">{{cite web |title=''Disphyma crassifolium'' (L.) L.Bolus |url=https://powo.science.kew.org/taxon/urn:lsid:ipni.org:names:361626-1 |publisher=Plants of the World Online |access-date=17 October 2020}}</ref>
* ''[[Disphyma dunsdonii]]'' <small>L.Bolus</small> that is endemic to the Cape Province;<ref name="POWO3">{{cite web |title=''Disphyma dunsdonii'' L.Bolus |url=https://powo.science.kew.org/taxon/urn:lsid:ipni.org:names:361627-1 |publisher=Plants of the World Online |access-date=17 October 2020}}</ref>
* ''[[Disphyma papillatum]]'' <small>[[Robert Chinnock|Chinnock]]</small> that is endemic to the [[Chatham Islands]] on New Zealand;<ref name="POWO4">{{cite web |title=''Disphyma papillatum'' Chinnock |url=https://powo.science.kew.org/taxon/urn:lsid:ipni.org:names:16167-1 |publisher=Plants of the World Online |access-date=17 October 2020}}</ref>

Plants of the World Online also accepts two subspecies:
* ''Disphyma australe'' subsp. ''stricticaule'' <small>Chinnock</small> that is endemic to [[Kermadec Island]] of New Zealand;<ref name="POWO5">{{cite web |title=''Disphyma australe'' subsp. ''stricticaule''|url=https://powo.science.kew.org/taxon/urn:lsid:ipni.org:names:874022-1 |publisher=Plants of the World Online |access-date=17 October 2020}}</ref>
* [[Disphyma crassifolium subsp. clavellatum|''Disphyma crassifolium'' subsp. ''clavellatum'']]<small> ([[Adrian Hardy Haworth|Haw.]]) Chinnock</small> that is endemic to Australia and has been introduced to the [[South Island]] of New Zealand.<ref name="POWO6">{{cite web |title=''Disphyma crassifolium'' subsp. ''clavellatum''|url=https://powo.science.kew.org/taxon/urn:lsid:ipni.org:names:953044-1 |publisher=Plants of the World Online |access-date=17 October 2020}}</ref>
